In [[mathematics]], '''essential dimension''' is an [[invariant (mathematics)|invariant]] defined for certain [[algebraic structure]]s such as [[algebraic group]]s and [[quadratic form]]s. It was introduced by [[Joe P. Buhler|Joe Buhler]] and [[Zinovy Reichstein]]<ref>{{cite journal |title=On the essential dimension of a finite group |journal=[[Compositio Mathematica]] |year=1997 |first1=J. |author1-link=Joe P. Buhler |last1=Buhler |last2=Reichstein |first2=Z. |author2-link=Zinovy Reichstein |volume=106 |issue=2 |pages=159–179 |doi=10.1023/A:1000144403695}}</ref> and in its full generality defined by [[Alexander Merkurjev]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=Essential dimension: A functorial point of view (after A. Merkurjev) |journal=[[Documenta Mathematica]] |year=2003 |first1=Grégory |last1=Berhuy |last2=Favi |first2=Giordano |volume=8 |pages=279–330 |doi=10.4171/DM/145 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Basically, essential dimension measures the complexity of algebraic structures via their [[field (mathematics)|fields]] of definition. For example, if <math>K</math> is a field and <math>V</math> a <math>K</math>-vector space, a [[quadratic form]] <math>q:V\to K</math> is said to be defined over a [[field extension|subfield]] <math>L</math> of <math>K</math> if there exists a <math>K</math>-[[basis (linear algebra)|basis]] <math>e_1,\dots,e_n</math> of <math>V</math> such that <math>q</math> can be expressed in the form
:<math>q\bigg(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i e_i\bigg) = \sum a_{ij} x_ix_j</math>
with all coefficients <math>a_{ij}</math> belonging to <math>L</math>. If <math>K</math> has [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] different from 2, every quadratic form is [[quadratic form#Equivalence of Quadratic Forms|diagonalizable]]. Therefore, <math>q</math> has a field of definition generated by <math>n</math> elements. Technically, one always works over a (fixed) base field <math>k</math> and the fields <math>K</math> and <math>L</math> in consideration are supposed to contain <math>k</math>. The essential dimension of <math>q</math> is then defined as the least [[transcendence degree]] over <math>k</math> of a subfield <math>L</math> of <math>K</math> over which <math>q</math> is defined.

==Formal definition==
Fix an arbitrary field <math>k</math> and let {{math|Fields}}<math>/k</math> denote the [[category (mathematics)|category]] of finitely generated [[field extension]]s of <math>k</math> with inclusions as [[morphism]]s. Consider a (covariant) [[functor]] <math>F:</math> {{math|Fields}}<math>/k\to</math> {{math|[[category of sets|Set]]}}.
For a field extension <math>K/k</math> and an element <math>a</math> of <math>F(K/k)</math> a ''field of definition of'' <math>a</math> is an [[intermediate field]] <math>K/L/k</math> such that <math>a</math> is contained in the image of the map <math>F(L/k)\to F(K/k)</math> induced by the inclusion of <math>L</math> in <math>K</math>.

The ''essential dimension of'' <math>a</math>, denoted by <math>\operatorname{ed}(a)</math>, is the least transcendence degree (over <math>k</math>) of a field of definition for <math>a</math>. The '''essential dimension of the functor ''F''''', denoted by <math>\operatorname{ed}(F)</math>, is the [[supremum]] of <math>\operatorname{ed}(a)</math> taken over all elements <math>a</math> of <math>F(K/k)</math> and objects <math>K/k</math> of {{math|Fields}}<math>/k</math>.

==Examples==
* Essential dimension of [[quadratic form]]s: For a [[natural number]] <math>n</math> consider the functor <math>Q_n:</math> {{math|Fields}}<math>/k\to</math> {{math|Set}} taking a field extension <math>K/k</math> to the set of [[isomorphism class]]es of non-degenerate <math>n</math>-dimensional quadratic forms over <math>K</math> and taking a morphism <math>L/k\to K/k</math> (given by the inclusion of <math>L</math> in <math>K</math>) to the map sending the isomorphism class of a quadratic form <math>q:V\to L</math> to the isomorphism class of the quadratic form <math>q_K : V \otimes_L K \to K</math>.

* Essential dimension of [[algebraic group]]s: for an algebraic group <math>G</math> over <math>k</math> denote by <math>H^1(-,G):</math> {{math|Fields}}<math>/k\to</math> {{math|Set}} the functor taking a field extension <math>K/k</math> to the set of isomorphism classes of <math>G</math>-[[torsor]]s over <math>K</math> (in the [[flat topology|fppf]]-topology). The essential dimension of this functor is called the ''essential dimension of the algebraic group'' <math>G</math>, denoted by <math>\operatorname{ed}(G)</math>.

* Essential dimension of a [[fibered category]]: let <math>\mathcal{F}</math> be a category fibered over the category <math>\operatorname{Aff}/k</math> of affine <math>k</math>-schemes, given by a functor <math>p : \mathcal{F} \to \operatorname{Aff}/k</math>. For example, <math>\mathcal{F}</math> may be the [[Moduli of algebraic curves|moduli stack]] <math>\mathcal{M}_g</math> of genus <math>g</math> curves or the classifying stack <math>\mathcal{BG}</math> of an algebraic group. Assume that for each <math>A\in\operatorname{Aff}/k</math> the isomorphism classes of objects in the fiber <math>p^{-1}(A)</math> form a set. Then we get a functor <math>F_p:</math> {{math|Fields}}<math>/k\to</math> {{math|Set}} taking a field extension <math>K/k</math> to the set of isomorphism classes in the fiber <math>p^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}(K))</math>. The essential dimension of the fibered category <math>\mathcal{F}</math> is defined as the essential dimension of the corresponding functor <math>F_p</math>. In the case of the classifying stack <math>\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{BG}</math> of an algebraic group <math>G</math>, the value coincides with the previously defined essential dimension of <math>G</math>.

==Known results==

* The essential dimension of a [[linear algebraic group]] <math>G</math> is always finite and bounded by the minimal dimension of a generically free [[representation (mathematics)|representation]] minus the dimension of <math>G</math>.

* For <math>G</math> a [[Spin group]] over an [[algebraically closed field]] <math>k</math>, the essential dimension is listed in {{OEIS2C|A280191}}.

* The essential dimension of a finite algebraic [[p-group|{{math|''p''}}-group]] over <math>k</math> equals the minimal dimension of a [[faithful representation]], provided that the base field <math>k</math> contains a primitive <math>p</math>-th [[root of unity]].

* The essential dimension of the [[symmetric group]] <math>S_n</math> (viewed as an algebraic group over <math>k</math>) is known for <math>n\leq 5</math> (for every base field <math>k</math>), for <math>n=6</math> (for <math>k</math> of characteristic not 2) and for <math>n=7</math> (in characteristic 0).

* Let <math>T</math> be an [[algebraic torus]] admitting a [[Galois field|Galois splitting field]] <math>L/k</math> of degree a power of a [[prime number|prime]] <math>p</math>. Then the essential dimension of <math>T</math> equals the least rank of the kernel of a [[homomorphism]] of <math>\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)</math>-[[lattice (group)|lattices]] <math>P\to X(T)</math> with [[cokernel]] finite and of order [[coprime]] to <math>p</math>, where <math>P</math> is a permutation lattice.
